1	# Task 12: Snowy mountain pass in a daytime blizzard
2	
3	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite. It must render one full-viewport canvas with id #app. The scene is a snowy mountain pass in a daytime blizzard. Show a V-shaped valley of white and blue-grey snow-covered slopes with exposed dark rock outcrops, a narrow trail winding up the middle marked by a line of 8 or more wooden poles, and a small wooden cabin with a snow-capped roof and a warm lit window halfway up the trail. Heavy wind-driven snow streaks across the scene at an angle with at least 1500 flakes in two sizes, gusts that periodically thicken the snow, and a flat pale-grey overcast sky. Distance fog turns far peaks into soft silhouettes. The camera slowly walks up the trail at about 1.7 m eye height with a slight sway and loops back to its start, with no user input. Do not rely on external downloads; build everything from simple shapes or procedural geometry.
4	
5	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
6	
7	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
8	
9	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
10	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
11	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
12	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict).

I'm thinking through how to render 1500 snow flakes efficiently—whether to use instanced meshes with per-frame transform updates, or a custom shader approach with billboarded quads animated via uTime, and planning to check the fire/water recipes for a similar pattern.

Also confirming createAuraApp works directly with a canvas element, so I want to check the recipes after 213, especially terrain and fire, for more guidance.

I need to figure out snow rendering next — since the requirement calls for at least 1500 flakes in two distinct sizes, I'm leaning toward building custom flake geometry with billboarded quads in two size groups rather than relying on built-in effect options.

Quads work better than points for GLSL sizing control, and I want flakes to streak at an angle, so I'm stretching each quad in screen space along its projected velocity direction, computing head and tail clip positions and expanding perpendicular to that line. The snow volume also needs to follow the camera, so I'm wrapping flake positions around `cameraPosition` using a modulo trick to keep them centered in a box ahead of the camera as it moves.

I'm centering the wrap box roughly 14 units forward along camera direction via an updated uniform each frame, since flakes behind the camera are wasted anyway. For gusts, I'm driving velocity multiplier, alpha, size, and streak length off a gust uniform, and varying visible flake density per-instance using a hash function so density increases with gust intensity, aiming for 1500+ total flakes split between small and large groups.

Fog stays static for now rather than coupling it to the atmosphere settings, though I want to double check that option later. I'm setting flakes to be transparent, white, with normal blending and no depth write, and I need to check how uniform types like vec3 are declared by looking at how the fire recipe handles its runtime-mutable uniforms.
